question: Why can two boxes both labelled kosher salt differ almost twofold in saltiness per spoonful?
answer: Crystal shape. Diamond Crystal grows hollow, flaky pyramids in open pans; Morton rolls dense cubes into flat flakes. A teaspoon of the first weighs about 3 g, of the second about 5, and both are nearly pure sodium chloride. A recipe tested with one and cooked with the other comes out oversalted or bland.
move: Measure by weight whenever the shape of the thing varies.
reference: Nosrat, Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat: Mastering the Elements of Good Cooking, Simon & Schuster, 2017
